options.title: Grimdark
options.description: Power is won with blood and kept with lies. Nobody stays clean, and the heroes are simply the people who haven't been caught yet.

options.title: Epic Quest
options.description: A long journey, a group of companions who shouldn't get along, and a goal that seems impossible. The fate of many rests on a few tired travellers.

options.title: Cosy Fantasy
options.description: Low stakes, warm kitchens and found family. The biggest danger might be a ruined festival, but it matters enormously to the people involved.

options.title: Dark Fairy Tale
options.description: Bargains with strange beings, rules that must never be broken, and a forest that remembers. Everything has a price, and it is always paid in full.

options.title: Mythic Epic
options.description: Gods walk among mortals, and their quarrels move mountains. Every act echoes for generations, and ordinary people are caught in games far bigger than themselves.

options.title: Sword and Sorcery
options.description: Fast, personal, sweaty adventure: a lone warrior or rogue, a treasure, and a dangerous rival who wants it too. Survive tonight; worry about tomorrow tomorrow.

options.title: Court Intrigue
options.description: Whispers in corridors, alliances sealed over dinner and broken by dawn. The sharpest weapon is information, and everyone is keeping score.

options.title: Tragic Fantasy
options.description: From the first page, we know someone will fall. The story is about why it happens, and whether anything good survives the fall.

options.title: Comic Fantasy
options.description: The world runs on paperwork, bad luck and misunderstandings. Ridiculous things are treated with total seriousness, and the jokes reveal something true.

options.title: Fantasy Mystery
options.description: Someone has died, disappeared, or stolen something that should be impossible to steal. A puzzle must be solved, and every clue makes the world stranger.

options.title: Folk Horror
options.description: A closed community with old customs that nobody explains to outsiders. Something is wrong beneath the friendly faces, and the land itself seems to be watching.

options.title: Coming of Age
options.description: Someone crosses a line they can never uncross: childhood, innocence, an old life. The world grows larger, certainties crack, and they must decide who to become.

options.title: No Magic
options.description: Magic does not exist and never has. Whatever people believe, the world runs on muscle, wit, weather and luck.

options.title: The Magic Is Gone
options.description: Magic vanished a generation ago. Its ruined wonders remain, and so do the people who still remember what it felt like.

options.title: Forbidden Art
options.description: Magic is real but outlawed. Anyone caught using it is punished harshly, so people with the gift hide it, sell it in secret, or become informers.

options.title: Magic Is a Con
options.description: Everyone believes in magic, but every wonder is a trick: chemistry, sleight of hand, clever lies. Some of the tricksters have started to believe their own act.

options.title: Magic of Cost
options.description: Every spell takes something from the caster: a memory, a year of life, the colour of their eyes. Great power leaves people hollow.

options.title: Song-Weaving
options.description: Magic is sung. Melodies shape stone, calm storms or rot wood, and a choir can do what no single voice would dare. Silence is a weapon.

options.title: Spirit Bargains
options.description: Nothing is cast; everything is negotiated. Spirits of rivers, roads and hearths grant favours, but they are moody, take words literally, and never forget a debt.

options.title: Living Ink
options.description: Words written or painted in rare pigments become true for as long as the writing survives. Scribes are powerful, and fire is feared.

options.title: Wild Surges
options.description: Magic happens by itself, in sudden bursts: a field turns to glass, a goat starts to speak. Nobody controls it; people simply try to live around it.

options.title: Inherited Gift
options.description: Only certain families carry magic, passed from parent to child. Their power has made them rulers, and their children are watched, guarded and married off for advantage.

options.title: Dream-Walking
options.description: Magic lives in sleep. A few people can enter the dreams of others to heal, spy or steal secrets, and the waking world is shaped by what happens there.

options.title: Ordinary Magic
options.description: Magic is common and a little boring: charms that keep milk fresh, fires that light on command. Everyone uses it, nobody thinks about it, and it often goes wrong.

options.title: Stone and Bone
options.description: Tools of flint, bone and wood. Fire is precious, the group is everything, and the nearest strangers may be a week's walk away.

options.title: Age of Bronze
options.description: The first cities, the first writing, the first organised armies. Bronze is rare and precious, chariots rule the battlefield, and kings claim heaven chose them.

options.title: Early Iron
options.description: Cheap iron tools have changed farming and war. Hill forts, river trade, and ambitious warlords rising where village elders once decided everything.

options.title: Roads and Aqueducts
options.description: An age of great engineering: paved roads, aqueducts, arched bridges and concrete. Armies, grain and news travel faster than ever before.

options.title: Castles and Mills
options.description: Stone castles, heavy ploughs, windmills and watermills. Most people farm, few can read, and a good sword costs more than a house.

options.title: Powder and Sail
options.description: Ocean-going ships, early cannons and the printing press. Maps still have blank edges, and new ideas spread faster than rulers would like.

options.title: Clockwork Age
options.description: Precise gears, springs and lenses. Mechanical clocks, telescopes and automatons fascinate the rich, and scholars argue whether the universe itself is a machine.

options.title: Steam and Smoke
options.description: Coal-fired engines, factories and the first railways. Cities swell with workers, the air turns grey, and old trades disappear within a decade.

options.title: Wire and Lightning
options.description: Electricity is new: telegraph lines, electric light, the first telephones. Messages cross continents in minutes, and many people find it deeply unnatural.

options.title: Engines and Airships
options.description: Combustion engines, early aircraft, radio broadcasts. The world feels suddenly small, and war can now reach anyone, anywhere.

options.title: After the Fall
options.description: A highly advanced civilisation collapsed long ago. People live with simple tools among ruins they don't understand, treating old machines as holy or cursed.

options.title: Uneven Progress
options.description: Wildly mixed technology: printing presses but no metal tools, or steam engines but no compass. One unexpected invention has changed everything around it.

options.title: Scattered Islands
options.description: Hundreds of small islands linked by canoes, trade winds and old family ties. The sea feeds everyone, and every year it takes someone.

options.title: Salt-Road Oasis
options.description: A walled oasis where desert trade routes cross. Water is wealth, guests are sacred, and every caravan brings rumours from distant lands.

options.title: Monsoon Delta
options.description: A maze of rivers, rice fields and houses on stilts. Life follows the rains: months of flood, months of drought, and festivals for both.

options.title: The Mountain Stair
options.description: A community carved into a cliff face, reached by a single narrow stair. Its leaders guard old knowledge and decide who may climb.

options.title: Land of Long Nights
options.description: A frozen land of endless winter nights and brief summers. Every family depends on the herds, the hunt and each other; exile means death.

options.title: City of a Million
options.description: A vast, crowded capital where a dozen languages are spoken on one street. You can buy anything here, including someone's silence.

options.title: Beneath the Earth
options.description: A network of caves and tunnels where people never see the sky. Light is grown, traded or stolen, and the deepest passages have never been mapped.

options.title: Rainforest Canopy
options.description: Villages built high in the trees of an ancient rainforest, joined by rope bridges. The forest floor below is dark, dangerous and rarely visited.

options.title: Open Steppe
options.description: Grassland to every horizon. The people move with their herds and carry their homes with them; borders mean nothing, and the sky means everything.

options.title: The Sinking City
options.description: A once-great city slowly sinking into the marsh. The rich live in the upper towers, everyone else wades, and the flooded streets hide forgotten things.

options.title: The Long Voyage
options.description: A single vessel on a long journey: a sea-ship, a river barge, or something stranger. Nobody can leave, and everyone knows everyone else's business.

options.title: Border Village
options.description: A small village on the frontier between two powers that both claim it. Families have relatives on each side, and loyalty is a daily decision.

options.title: Healer
options.description: Someone who mends bodies, with herbs, knives or prayer. They see people at their weakest and know more secrets than any spy.

options.title: Deserter
options.description: A soldier who walked away from their army. Some call it cowardice, some call it conscience. Their old comrades are still looking for them.

options.title: Thief with a Code
options.description: A skilled thief with strict personal rules about who they will and won't steal from. Those rules are about to be tested.

options.title: Unwilling Heir
options.description: Next in line to lead a family, clan, guild or nation, and wishing they weren't. Everyone has plans for them; they have only doubts.

options.title: Keeper of Memory
options.description: Keeper of a community's history, in books, songs or knotted cords. They know the official story, and they know exactly where it is wrong.

options.title: Travelling Trader
options.description: Buys low, sells high, and moves on before trouble arrives. Speaks a little of many languages and trusts nobody completely.

options.title: Retired Executioner
options.description: Carried out the harshest sentences of the law for twenty years. Now they want a quiet life, but the faces of the condemned have not gone away.

options.title: Apprentice
options.description: Halfway through learning a craft from a demanding master. Not ready to work alone, but circumstances are about to force them.

options.title: The Stranger
options.description: Newly arrived from far away, with unfamiliar clothes, manners and beliefs. Nobody here understands them, and they don't understand anybody either.

options.title: Desperate Parent
options.description: An ordinary person with a child to protect, ready to do anything to keep that child safe. Ordinary people can become very dangerous.

options.title: Impostor
options.description: Living under a false identity, perhaps a dead noble's name or a forged rank. The lie has lasted for years. Someone has just recognised them.

options.title: Gatekeeper
options.description: Decides who gets in and who stays out: at a city gate, a border or a temple door. Bribes are offered daily; refusing them has a cost.

options.title: Debt of Blood
options.description: Someone the character loved was wronged, and the person responsible is now powerful and protected. Revenge is possible, but it will cost everything.

options.title: Hunger Season
options.description: The food will run out long before the next harvest or hunt. Someone must decide who eats, who leaves, and who goes searching for help that may not exist.

options.title: A Loving Lie
options.description: The character discovers that the person they trust most has lied to them for years, and that the lie was meant to protect them.

options.title: Divided Loyalty
options.description: Two people the character loves stand on opposite sides of a conflict. Choosing one means losing the other; refusing to choose may lose both.

options.title: The Wrong Prophecy
options.description: Everyone believes an old prophecy names the character as saviour or destroyer. The character knows it is a mistake, but nobody will listen.

options.title: Something Is Coming
options.description: A powerful outside force is approaching: an army, a rival nation, something nobody understands. The community must choose to fight, flee, bargain or surrender.

options.title: Someone Is Missing
options.description: A person vanished without a trace three days ago. The character is the only one who believes they are still alive.

options.title: The Witness
options.description: The character saw something they were never supposed to see. Now powerful people want them silent, and nobody believes their story.

options.title: An Old Promise
options.description: Years ago the character swore an oath. Today the person they swore it to has come to collect, and keeping the promise means doing something terrible.

options.title: The Offer of Power
options.description: The character is offered real power: a seat, a title, a crown. To take it, they must become the kind of person they have always despised.

options.title: The Impossible Task
options.description: The character must complete a ridiculous task before a deadline: win a contest, deliver a parcel, build something nobody has built. Failure will be very public.

options.title: Get Out Alive
options.description: The character is trapped (imprisoned, besieged or lost) and must escape with companions who slow them down, disagree with them, or can't be trusted.
